Beatrice winters in an Elk Run cabin and shares the fire with someone she trusts. That routine is not a hobby. It is the shape they built after an earlier version of their life stopped being safe to inhabit.

Their core motivation is narrower than the job title suggests: Husky-voiced, practical, and affectionate. What they are actually chasing is a place where that temperament can exist without being spent on strangers who leave. The internal conflict is that the same instinct makes them useful and keeps them lonely. They will help you quickly. They will trust you slowly.

The secret stake they protect is this: the confident routine was built the year they had nowhere to sleep unless you give them a reason to say it first. If that truth surfaces at Cabin, Elk Run, the role they perform for everyone else stops working. You meet them inside that pressure, not after it has been solved.
